API Reference

main

main.main() → None[source]

Entry point: parse CLI args, build the dataset, and run the SFS pipeline.

Builds a ShapeFromShadingDataset from --images-dir/--masks-dir and hands it, along with the rest of the parsed flags, to src.run.run().

main.parse_args() → Namespace[source]

Build and parse the command-line interface for running Shape-from-Shading.

Returns:

Parsed CLI arguments, one attribute per flag (e.g. args.images_dir, args.num_iters), ready to be passed into src.run.run().

Return type:

argparse.Namespace

src.config

class src.config.SFSConfig(image_path: str, num_iters: int = 2000, lambda_smooth: float = 1.0, lr: float = 0.01, optimize_light: bool = True, light_direction: torch.Tensor | None = None, save_to: str | None = None, optimize_albedo: bool = False, use_mask: bool = False, init_kind: Literal['init_grads', 'zeroes', 'ones', 'sphere'] = 'init_grads', desc: str | None = None, parametrization_type: Literal['cartesian', 'stereographic'] = 'stereographic')[source]

Configuration for a single Shape-from-Shading optimization run.

One SFSConfig is built per object in src.run.run() and passed straight into src.sfs.shape_from_shading().

desc: str | None = None

Optional free-text description of the run.

image_path: str

Path to the grayscale input image.

Strategy used to initialize the normal map; see utils.initializations.get_init().

lambda_smooth: float = 1.0

Weight of the normal-smoothness regularizer.

light_direction: torch.Tensor | None = None

Initial light direction as a 3-vector; if None, src.core_utils.get_light_direction() supplies a default.

lr: float = 0.01

Learning rate for the Adam optimizer.

num_iters: int = 2000

Number of optimizer steps to run.

optimize_albedo: bool = False

Whether albedo is jointly optimized.

optimize_light: bool = True

Whether the light direction is a learnable parameter.

parametrization_type: Literal['cartesian', 'stereographic'] = 'stereographic'

Whether normals are optimized directly ("cartesian") or via a stereographic projection ("stereographic").

src.core_utils

src.core_utils.build_optimizer(cfg: SFSConfig, optim_var: torch.nn.Parameter, light_dir_: torch.Tensor, device: Literal['cuda', 'mps', 'cpu']) → Tuple[torch.optim.Optimizer, torch.Tensor, torch.nn.Parameter | None][source]

Build the Adam optimizer, selecting which quantities are learnable.

optim_var (the normal-map parameter being optimized) is always included. Whether light_dir_ and/or albedo are also added as learnable parameters depends on cfg.optimize_light and cfg.optimize_albedo.

Parameters:

  • cfg – The run’s config; reads cfg.optimize_light, cfg.optimize_albedo, and cfg.lr.

  • optim_var – The primary tensor being optimized (raw normals or stereographic (f, g) parameters), already wrapped as a torch.nn.Parameter.

  • light_dir – Initial light direction, e.g. from get_light_direction().

  • device – Device to place the albedo parameter on.

Returns:

(opt, light_dir, albedo) where

  • opt is the configured torch.optim.Adam instance.

  • light_dir is a learnable torch.nn.Parameter if cfg.optimize_light is True, otherwise the original light_dir_ tensor (not optimized).

  • albedo is a torch.nn.Parameter initialized to 1.0 (always created, but only included in opt when cfg.optimize_albedo is True).

Return type:

tuple

src.core_utils.get_light_direction(cfg: SFSConfig, device: Literal['cuda', 'mps', 'cpu']) → torch.Tensor[source]

Resolve the initial light direction to use for a run.

Parameters:

  • cfg – The run’s config. If cfg.light_direction is set, that value is used; otherwise a default is returned.

  • device – Device the returned tensor should live on.

Returns:

A 3-vector light direction on device, either cfg.light_direction or the default [0.0, 0.0, 1.0].

Return type:

torch.Tensor

src.core_utils.l2_smoothness(x: torch.Tensor, mask: torch.Tensor | None = None) → torch.Tensor[source]

Compute a smoothness regularizer: the mean squared spatial gradient of x.

Parameters:

  • x – Tensor of shape (H, W, ...) whose spatial smoothness is penalized (e.g. a normal map).

  • mask – Optional boolean/float mask of shape (H, W). When given, x is zeroed outside the mask before taking gradients, so the loss is only (approximately) computed within the masked region.

Returns:

Scalar loss, the mean of grad_x**2 and grad_y**2.

Return type:

torch.Tensor

src.core_utils.normalize_normals(n: torch.Tensor) → torch.Tensor[source]

Normalize per-pixel normals to unit length along the last dimension.

Parameters:

n – Normal map of shape (H, W, 3) (unnormalized).

Returns:

Normal map of the same shape, with each pixel’s normal vector rescaled to unit norm (a small epsilon avoids division by zero).

Return type:

torch.Tensor

src.sfs

src.sfs.shape_from_shading(cfg: SFSConfig, mask_pth: str, use_wandb: bool = False, log_intermediates: bool = False)[source]

Main SFS optimization loop.

Loads the image/mask, initializes a normal map, and optimizes it (plus optionally light direction and albedo) by gradient descent on a Lambertian reflectance loss with a smoothness regularizer: loss = (R - I)^2 + lambda_smooth * l2_smoothness(n), where R = max(0, n . L) is the predicted reflectance.

Parameters:

  • cfg – Run configuration; see SFSConfig.

  • mask_pth – Path to the binary mask image for cfg.image_path.

  • use_wandb – If True, logs per-iteration losses to Weights & Biases.

  • log_intermediates – If True, saves a normal-map snapshot every 200 iterations to {cfg.save_to}/normals{it}.png.

Returns:

(normals, reflectance, mask) where

  • normals is the optimized, mask-zeroed normal map, shape (H, W, 3), on CPU.

  • reflectance is the predicted reflectance map, shape (H, W), on CPU.

  • mask is the boolean mask as a numpy array, shape (H, W).

Return type:

tuple

src.run

src.run.run(dataset: ShapeFromShadingDataset, out_path: str = 'out', target: str | None = None, num_iters: int = 2000, lr: float = 0.01, lambda_smooth: float = 1.0, optimize_light: bool = True, light_direction: torch.Tensor = torch.tensor, optimize_albedo: bool = False, init_kind: Literal['init_grads', 'zeroes', 'ones', 'sphere'] = 'init_grads', parametrization_type: Literal['cartesian', 'stereographic'] = 'cartesian', use_wandb: bool = False, log_intermediates: bool = False)[source]

Run Shape-from-Shading over one or all objects in dataset.

For each selected object, builds an SFSConfig, runs src.sfs.shape_from_shading(), and saves the results via save_results() into {out_path}/{object_name}/.

Parameters:

  • dataset – Indexed image/mask pairs to run on.

  • out_path – Base output directory; a subfolder is created per object.

  • target – If given, only this object is run; otherwise every object in dataset is run.

  • num_iters – Number of optimizer iterations per object.

  • lr – Learning rate for the Adam optimizer.

  • lambda_smooth – Weight of the normal-smoothness regularizer.

  • optimize_light – Whether to jointly optimize the light direction.

  • light_direction – Initial light direction, shape (3,).

  • optimize_albedo – Whether to jointly optimize albedo.

  • init_kind – Strategy used to initialize the normal map.

  • parametrization_type – Whether normals are optimized directly ("cartesian") or via a stereographic projection ("stereographic").

  • use_wandb – Whether to log losses to Weights & Biases.

  • log_intermediates – Whether to periodically save intermediate normal maps during optimization.

src.run.save_results(folder: str, normals: torch.Tensor, reflectance: torch.Tensor, mask: numpy.ndarray) → None[source]

Save normals (png/npy/pt), integrated depth (pt/png/html), and reflectance (png) for a single object’s result into folder.

Also integrates the normals into a depth map (via utils.integrator.integrate_normals()) before saving it.

Parameters:

  • folder – Output directory for this object’s result files.

  • normals – Final normal map, shape (H, W, 3).

  • reflectance – Final reflectance map, shape (H, W).

  • mask – Boolean mask of valid pixels, shape (H, W).

src.eval.evaluate_objects(objects: list[str], out_path: str, gt_dir: str = 'GT_data4/Normals', mask_dir: str = 'GT_data4/Masks', direct_pred_dir: str = 'out_ananta/Cue1', stereo_pred_dir: str = 'stereo_outputs/Cue1')[source]

Loop over objects, compute metrics for each prediction type, and save a single combined metrics.json using log().

For each object, loads its ground-truth normals/mask and two sets of predicted normals (“direct” and “stereo”), then scores each against the ground truth with compute_metrics().

Parameters:

  • objects – Object basenames to evaluate (e.g. ["sphere", "cube"]).

  • out_path – Directory to write the combined metrics.json to.

  • gt_dir – Directory containing ground-truth normal maps ({gt_dir}/{obj}.png).

  • mask_dir – Directory containing masks ({mask_dir}/{obj}.png).

  • direct_pred_dir – Directory containing direct-normal-estimation predictions ({direct_pred_dir}/{obj}/normals.npy).

  • stereo_pred_dir – Directory containing stereographic-parametrization predictions ({stereo_pred_dir}/{obj}/normals.npy).

Returns:

Maps each object name to {"direct": {...}, "stereo": {...}} metrics dicts (see compute_metrics()).

Return type:

dict

Write a metrics dict to {path}/metrics.json, creating path if needed.

Parameters:

utils.initializations

utils.initializations.compute_gradients(image: numpy.ndarray) → Tuple[numpy.ndarray, numpy.ndarray][source]

Use Scharr filters to get image gradients.

Parameters:

image – Grayscale image array of shape (H, W).

Returns:

(grad_x, grad_y), each of shape (H, W), the Scharr-filtered gradients in x and y.

Return type:

Tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]

utils.initializations.compute_normals_from_gradients(grad_x: numpy.ndarray, grad_y: numpy.ndarray) → numpy.ndarray[source]

Convert surface gradients (p, q) to unit surface normals.

Uses the standard shape-from-shading convention n = normalize([-p, -q, 1]).

Parameters:

  • grad_x – Gradient in x (p), shape (H, W).

  • grad_y – Gradient in y (q), shape (H, W).

Returns:

Unit normal map of shape (H, W, 3).

Return type:

np.ndarray

utils.initializations.get_init(shape: Tuple[int, int], image_np: numpy.ndarray | None = None, kind: Literal['init_grads', 'zeroes', 'sphere', 'ones'] = 'init_grads', device: str | None = None)[source]

Initialize a learnable normal map for the optimization loop.

Parameters:

  • shape – (H, W) spatial shape of the normal map to create.

  • image_np – Grayscale input image, required when kind="init_grads" (used to compute an image-gradient-based initialization).

  • kind –

    Initialization strategy:

    • "init_grads": Estimate normals from the image’s Scharr gradients (via compute_gradients() and compute_normals_from_gradients()); usually the best starting point.

    • "zeroes": Near-flat normals pointing at the viewer (z ~= 0.99) plus a little noise.

    • "ones": All-ones tensor (not unit-normalized).

    • "sphere": A synthetic hemisphere bulging toward the viewer.

  • device – Device to create the tensor on; defaults to utils.utils.get_device().

Returns:

A (H, W, 3) tensor with requires_grad=True, ready to be wrapped in (or used directly as) an optimizer parameter.

Return type:

torch.Tensor

Raises:

ValueError – If kind is not one of the supported strategies.

utils.integrator

utils.integrator.integrate_normals(normals: numpy.ndarray, x_range: Tuple[float, float] = (-1.0, 1.0), y_range: Tuple[float, float] = (-1.0, 1.0))[source]

Integrate a normal map into a depth map via Poisson/DCT integration.

Converts normals to surface gradients (p, q), scales them into world units given x_range/y_range, robustifies them (clip + blur, via utils.initializations._robustify_pq()), and integrates with _poisson_integration().

Parameters:

  • normals – Normal map of shape (H, W, 3).

  • x_range – World-space (min, max) extent of the image in x.

  • y_range – World-space (min, max) extent of the image in y.

Returns:

Depth map of shape (H, W).

Return type:

np.ndarray

utils.stereo_maps

utils.stereo_maps.fg_to_normals(fg: torch.Tensor) → torch.Tensor[source]

Convert stereographic parameters (f, g) back to unit normals.

Inverts normals_to_fg() via the standard stereographic projection formula, so normals can be optimized in an unconstrained 2D space (f, g) while always mapping back to valid unit vectors.

Parameters:

fg – Tensor of shape (..., 2) holding stereographic parameters (f, g) in its last dimension.

Returns:

Unit normal map of shape (..., 3).

Return type:

torch.Tensor

utils.stereo_maps.normals_to_fg(normals: torch.Tensor) → torch.Tensor[source]

Convert unit normals to stereographic parameters (f, g).

Normals are first renormalized to unit length, then projected via f = 2*nx / (1 + nz), g = 2*ny / (1 + nz). This is the inverse of fg_to_normals().

Parameters:

normals – Normal map of shape (..., 3).

Returns:

Stereographic parameters of shape (..., 2).

Return type:

torch.Tensor

utils.normals_from_depth

utils.normals_from_depth.calculate_normals_numpy(depth_map: numpy.ndarray, mask: numpy.ndarray) → numpy.ndarray[source]

Compute surface normals from a depth map, restricted to a mask.

Lightly Gaussian-smooths the depth map, takes its spatial gradients, and converts them to unit normals (n = normalize([-p, -q, 1])). Pixels outside mask are zeroed out.

Parameters:

  • depth_map – Depth map of shape (H, W).

  • mask – Boolean region-of-interest mask of shape (H, W).

Returns:

Normal map of shape (H, W, 3), zeroed outside mask.

Return type:

np.ndarray

utils.plotting.plotting.plot_depth_3d_plotly(depth: torch.Tensor | numpy.ndarray, save_path: str | Path | None = None, show: bool = False, log: bool = False, normalize_xyz: bool = False, mask: torch.Tensor | numpy.ndarray | None = None, hide_invalid: bool = True)[source]

Render a depth map as an interactive 3D surface with Plotly.

The depth map is downsampled (every 8th pixel) for a lighter-weight plot. If hide_invalid is set, mask is required and invalid (masked out) pixels are set to NaN so they render as gaps in the surface.

Parameters:

  • depth – Depth map, shape (H, W).

  • save_path – If given, saves the plot as an interactive HTML file at this path.

  • show – If True, opens the plot in a browser via fig.show().

  • log – If True, renders the figure to a PNG and logs it to wandb.

  • normalize_xyz – If True, rescales X, Y, and depth into [0, 1].

  • mask – Boolean mask of valid pixels; required when hide_invalid is True.

  • hide_invalid – If True, masks out invalid pixels as NaN (gaps) in the surface. Requires mask.

Raises:

AssertionError – If hide_invalid is True but mask is None.

utils.plotting.plotting.plot_image(img: numpy.ndarray | torch.Tensor, title: str | None = None, save_path: str | Path | None = None, show: bool = False, cmap: str | None = None, hide_axis: bool = False, pad_inches: float = 0.0) → None[source]

utils.plotting.plotting.plot_normals(normals: numpy.ndarray | torch.Tensor, save_path: str | Path | None = None, show: bool = False, mask: numpy.ndarray | torch.Tensor | None = None, title: str | None = None) → None[source]

Plot a normal map, visualized as an RGB image.

Converts normals to the [0, 1] RGB visualization range (via utils.plotting.helpers.normals_to_rgb()) and, if mask is given, sets pixels outside the mask to NaN so they render as blank. For a per-component (X/Y/Z) view instead, see plot_component_normals().

Parameters:

  • normals – Normal map with a trailing channel dim of size 3.

  • save_path – If given, the figure is saved to this path.

  • show – If True, displays the figure.

  • mask – Optional boolean mask of valid pixels.

  • title – Optional axes title.

utils.plotting.helpers.save_or_show(fig: matplotlib.figure.Figure, save_path: str | Path | None = None, show: bool = False, pad_inches: float = 0.0) → None[source]

Handle saving and/or showing a matplotlib figure. if show is true, it shows the plot. When save plath is available, it saves it to path

Parameters:

  • fig – The matplotlib figure to save/show.

  • save_path – If given, the figure is saved to this path.

  • show – If True, displays the figure via plt.show(); otherwise it is closed (to free memory) after any save.

  • pad_inches – Padding passed to fig.savefig.
